Who sends the Baton Rouge property tax bill, and who sets the amount?

In Baton Rouge, the East Baton Rouge Parish Assessor sets the value, and the East Baton Rouge Parish Sheriff, acting as tax collector, mails the bill and takes the payment. The Sheriff's own FAQ says it does not decide how much you owe: your bill is the assessed value times the millage rates attached to your property, and the parish voters approve the millages.

Baton Rouge is a consolidated city-parish, so one tax notice can carry parish levies, city levies and several district charges. The Sheriff's FAQ says all cities in the parish except Central collect city taxes on the same notice, which includes Baton Rouge, Baker and Zachary.

Who values the property?EBR Parish AssessorLocated in City Hall, Room 126, phone (225) 389-3920
Who bills and collects?EBR Parish Sheriff, Tax DepartmentCity Hall, 2nd Floor, 222 Saint Louis Street, Room 238; (225) 389-4810
In-person hoursSheriff's tax counterMonday to Friday, 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM

Where is Baton Rouge, and why does the ground matter for a house?

Baton Rouge is the capital of Louisiana, sitting on the east bank of the Mississippi River about 79 miles from New Orleans. Wikipedia's summary reports a 2020 census population of 227,470, which makes it the second-largest city in the state, and a Greater Baton Rouge metro of 870,569.

The city grew on the Istrouma Bluff, the first natural bluff upriver from the Mississippi delta. The bluff let early settlers build away from seasonal river flooding, and a levee system later extended south from it.

Wikipedia puts the average rainfall at about 62 inches a year, which makes Baton Rouge one of the wettest large cities in the country. It also records that Hurricane Gustav hit the city on September 1, 2008, with winds above 100 miles per hour that dropped trees and power lines and damaged many roofs.

What drives the Baton Rouge economy?

State government, two large universities, a major river port and heavy industry carry most of the local economy. Louisiana State University and Southern University are both based in the city, and the Port of Greater Baton Rouge is described as the tenth-largest in the United States by tonnage. It is also the farthest point upstream on the Mississippi that can take ocean-going tankers and cargo carriers.

The same source lists Lamar Advertising, BBQGuys, Marucci Sports, Piccadilly Restaurants and Raising Cane's as companies headquartered in the city, and notes Amazon and Microsoft offices in the area. Petrochemical, medical, research and film work are also named.

How is a Baton Rouge home assessed?

The assessor takes the estimated market value, analyzes sales of similar homes nearby, and assesses a residential property at 10% of that value. The Assessor's page gives a worked example: a $175,000 house (land $35,000, house $140,000) has a total assessed value of $17,500. At an illustration rate of 89.50 mills, parish tax comes to $1,566.25 without a homestead exemption.

The same page notes that commercial buildings are assessed at 15% of market value, which is why a rental-heavy block can show a different tax pattern from an owner-occupied one. Millage also varies by location within the parish. Property inside city limits usually shares one rate, apart from the downtown development district, the levee district and the Comite River Diversion Canal district. Property outside the city can carry extra millages for fire protection, road lighting, garbage and the canal.

Step in the Assessor's exampleAmount
Market value of land plus house$175,000
Assessed value at 10%$17,500
Parish tax at 89.50 mills, no exemption$1,566.25
Net assessed value with $7,500 homestead exemption$10,000
Parish tax at 89.50 mills with exemption$895.00

These figures are the office's illustration with an arbitrary rate. Your own notice shows your rates.

What does the homestead exemption cover in East Baton Rouge Parish?

The homestead exemption removes parish tax on the first $75,000 of market value, which is $7,500 of assessed value, for the home you own and live in. The Sheriff's FAQ adds that it does not apply to city taxes or to fire and crime district fees.

The Assessor's general information page says the exemption is worth roughly $750 to $800 a year, depending on assessed value and the millage in your area. You must own and occupy the home by December 31 of the tax year, and you do not reapply each year unless the title changes.

Extra relief exists for some owners:

  • Veterans with a service-connected disability rating of 50% through 69% get an additional $2,500 of assessed value exempt, and 70% through 99% get $4,500. A 100% rating exempts the full assessed value from parish tax, though city taxes and fees stay on the bill.
  • The special assessment level freezes the assessed value for an owner aged 65 or older who owns, occupies and has a homestead exemption, with total adjusted gross income not above $102,700.

What are the Baton Rouge property tax dates?

The Baton Rouge cycle starts on January 1 and ends with payment by December 31. The Assessor's dates page and the Sheriff's FAQ together give this calendar.

DateWhat happens
January 1Property is assessed for condition and ownership as of this date
April 1Business personal property self-reporting forms due
August 15 to September 15Tax roll open for public inspection for 15 days; exact dates are published in the Advocate
November 15Louisiana Tax Commission certifies the roll; the Sheriff mails notices shortly after, usually the last week of November
December 31Taxes due; delinquent after this date, with interest at 1% per month

The Sheriff accepts a postmark as proof of payment only when the U.S. Postal Service actually canceled the envelope.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How do you challenge a Baton Rouge assessment?

You review the value while the books are open, then take the dispute to the Metro Council sitting as the board of review. During the 15-calendar-day inspection window the assessor's staff can discuss discrepancies in value. The Assessor says a call after August 1 reveals that year's open dates.

If the Metro Council agrees with the assessor or with the owner, either side can appeal to the Louisiana Tax Commission. The page gives no separate board of review deadline, so ask the office for the current year's dates.

What happens to Baton Rouge property tax when a house is sold?

At a Baton Rouge closing the taxes are settled, not paid. The Assessor's general information page uses that exact phrase, and the Sheriff's FAQ explains the reason: the tax collector does not prorate a bill between buyer and seller, and any deal the two make about tax is a private matter. Unpaid tax, interest and fees stay with the property until someone pays them.

Louisiana law puts the bill in the name of whoever owned the property on January 1. The Sheriff's FAQ says that if you buy after that date, the notice may still go to the prior owner, and the new owner is responsible for checking whether anything is owed. A buyer can ask the Sheriff for a tax certificate showing that taxes are paid, and the Assessor's page recommends an abstract of title and title insurance.

  • Ask the Sheriff's Tax Office at (225) 389-4810 for the balance before you sign a sale contract.
  • If a mortgage company escrows your taxes, ask it for proof of payment. The Sheriff posts the first payment it receives and will not reverse a duplicate.
  • Once the title changes, the new owner has to sign a fresh homestead application with the closing papers.

The unpaid-tax rules have recently changed. The Bossier Parish Sheriff's site explains that from January 1, 2026, Louisiana tax collectors sell a tax lien certificate at the annual auction rather than the property itself. The East Baton Rouge Sheriff's page lists a 2026 online tax lien auction for July 8, though other text on its FAQ still describes the older tax sale and redemption steps. Treat a delinquent balance as urgent and confirm the current process with the Sheriff.

Can you sell a Baton Rouge house that owes back taxes?

Yes. A house with tax due can still be sold, as long as the title company pays the balance from the sale proceeds at closing. The cleaner your numbers are before you list or accept an offer, the fewer surprises appear at the table.

Owners in Baton Rouge often run into the same few issues when taxes are behind: a homestead exemption that lapsed after an inheritance, a mailing address that was never updated so notices went to a relative, or a mortgage escrow account that was not funded. Anyone behind on a Baton Rouge bill should call the Sheriff first, then talk to a title company or attorney about the payoff.

More questions about Baton Rouge, LA Property Tax Guide

Who do I pay property tax to in Baton Rouge?

You pay the East Baton Rouge Parish Sheriff, who is the tax collector. You can pay online through the link on the Sheriff's site, mail the payment with the stub, or pay in person at City Hall, 2nd Floor, 222 Saint Louis Street, Room 238, from 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM on weekdays. The Assessor's Office does not accept payment.

When are Baton Rouge property taxes due?

Taxes are due by December 31 each year and are delinquent after that date, with interest at 1% per month. The Sheriff usually mails notices during the last week of November.

Does the Baton Rouge homestead exemption lower my city tax?

No. The exemption removes parish tax on the first $75,000 of market value ($7,500 assessed), but it does not apply to city taxes or to fire and crime district fees.

Do buyer and seller split the tax bill at a Baton Rouge closing?

The tax collector does not prorate between buyer and seller. Any sharing of the bill is a private arrangement handled at closing, and the full bill remains owed to the Sheriff until paid.

How do I appeal my Baton Rouge assessment?

Review the assessment during the open-roll period, which runs 15 calendar days between August 15 and September 15, then bring the complaint to the Metro Council sitting as the board of review. Either side can then appeal to the Louisiana Tax Commission. Call the Assessor after August 1 for that year's exact dates.

Can I sell my Baton Rouge house if I owe tax?

Yes, as long as the unpaid tax, interest and fees are paid from the proceeds at closing. Get the current payoff from the Sheriff's Tax Office before you agree to a closing date.

Which parish bills property tax in Shreveport?

Caddo Parish bills most Shreveport houses, because the city is the Caddo Parish seat, but part of Shreveport reaches into Bossier Parish. Wikipedia explains that the city extends along the west bank of the Red River into Bossier Parish, and that the Bossier portions are served by the Bossier Parish School District.

Before you search for a bill, check which parish your parcel is in. Most owners are in Caddo. A house on the Bossier side deals with the Bossier Parish assessor and tax collector instead.

Shreveport was founded in 1836 by the Shreve Town Company and incorporated on March 20, 1839. Caddo Parish was created in 1838, and the parish covers 937 square miles in the northwest corner of Louisiana.

Where do you go in Shreveport to look up or pay property tax?

Both Caddo offices share one building: 501 Texas Street in downtown Shreveport. The Assessor is in Room 102, and the Sheriff's tax division is in Room 101.

OfficeRoleContact
Caddo Parish AssessorValues property, handles homestead exemption filings501 Texas Street, Room 102, 318.226.6704, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. weekdays
Caddo Parish Sheriff, Tax DivisionBills and collects the tax501 Texas Street, Room 101, (318) 675-2170

The Assessor's site offers a free property search by owner name, section, township and range, or subdivision, with GIS maps. A day pass for deeper searches costs $10, and a professional subscription is $35 a month, according to the Assessor's page.

The Sheriff's site takes payments online, and online tax payments post the same day until 11:59 p.m. It also lists a pre-payment program and links to delinquent properties and sheriff sales.

When is Shreveport property tax due and what happens if it is late?

Louisiana taxes are due December 31, and unpaid tax earns 1% interest per month, according to the House Fiscal Division's property tax summary. Each December the parish tax collector sends owners a bill listing the millages and the amount due.

If the tax stays unpaid, the tax collector can sell the property at a tax sale. The House summary says an owner of property sold this way has three years to redeem it, and that is a long window, but the debt grows meanwhile. A notice of delinquency is a good reason to call the Sheriff's tax division the same week.

The Caddo Sheriff's page did not list its own interest or fee schedule, so ask the office for a payoff figure instead of estimating one. A written payoff is also what a title company will need for a sale.

What does Shreveport's size and layout mean for tax and sales?

Shreveport covers about 124 square miles, of which roughly 108 are land, and Wikipedia gives its 2020 census population as 187,593. The 2024 Census estimate is 176,578, below the historic high of 206,989 in 1980.

The city sits at 236 feet of elevation on the west bank of the Red River. Its western and northern portions are low and close to the river, so flood-zone checks matter for those parcels more than for houses on higher ground.

The parish also contains Bethany, Dixie, Keithville, Mira and other small places outside the city. A house with a Shreveport mailing address may sit in one of them, which can change the tax bill, so read the parcel record instead of trusting the postal name.

Caddo Public Schools serves all of Caddo Parish, including the Shreveport sections. The colleges named include Centenary College, LSU Shreveport and Southern University at Shreveport, and the LSU Health Sciences Center medical school opened in 1969.

How are Shreveport homes assessed and how do you appeal?

Residential property is assessed at 10% of fair market value, and a taxpayer who disagrees can appeal to the local Board of Review. The state describes residential 10%, commercial 15% and public service 25% as the assessment ratios.

The assessment roll is open for inspection in most parishes between August 15 and September 15. That is the time to look at your parcel card and compare it with similar houses near you.

  • Check the square footage, bedroom count and year built on the parcel card.
  • Look for exemptions you may have missed.
  • Ask the Assessor how to file with the Board of Review, since the Assessor's front page did not describe the appeal steps.

The homestead exemption applies to $7,500 of assessed value, or $75,000 of fair market value. In Caddo, homeowners can apply for it online through the parcel card on the Assessor's property search. Owners 65 and older should ask the Assessor about the special assessment freeze.

What should Shreveport sellers know about weather and house age?

Shreveport has a humid subtropical climate, and severe thunderstorms, hail, damaging winds and tornadoes are part of spring and summer. Annual precipitation normally tops 51 inches, and the city sees about 91 days a year above 90 degrees.

That mix is hard on roofs and cooling systems. Wikipedia also notes about 35 days a year at or below freezing, with ice and sleet possible, and a record of 110 degrees on August 25 and 26, 2023.

The Census Bureau's 2019 to 2023 survey puts the median year built for Shreveport homes at 1973, so many houses are fifty years old or more. Buyers' inspectors tend to look first at the roof, the HVAC unit, the plumbing and the electrical panel.

  • Keep roof receipts and any storm claim paperwork.
  • Note the age of your air conditioner.
  • Write down any past leaks so the disclosure you give is accurate.

What drives the Shreveport economy and neighborhoods?

Healthcare, schools, government, distribution and the nearby Air Force base anchor Shreveport's economy. Wikipedia's Caddo Parish page lists its largest 2017 employers as Caddo Parish Public Schools with 9,416 jobs, Willis-Knighton Medical Center with 6,732, University Health with 6,372, LSU Health Shreveport with 2,762 and the City of Shreveport with 2,569.

Barksdale Air Force Base sits in Bossier Parish and hosts Air Force Global Strike Command and the 2d Bomb Wing. The General Motors Shreveport plant closed in August 2012, and Amazon began a $200 million fulfillment center in 2021.

Neighborhoods named on Wikipedia include Broadmoor, Caddo Heights, Pierremont, Highland, Lakeside, Mooretown and Ledbetter Heights. The Youree Drive area, the downtown riverfront and Highland are described as busy parts of the city.

Interstate 20 crosses the city, I-220 forms the north loop, and Louisiana Highway 3132 is the Inner Loop. Shreveport Regional Airport is served by Allegiant, American, Delta and United Express.

What happens to property tax when you sell a Shreveport house?

The title company pays unpaid tax from the sale proceeds, and the Louisiana deed must name the person responsible for property taxes and a mailing address for notices. That second point comes from La. R.S. 9:2721 and is easy to forget on a hurried closing.

Ask for a current payoff from the Sheriff before closing day. If the sale is in November or December, the new bill may already be on its way, so settle in writing who covers the year.

A transfer of a house must be made by authentic act or act under private signature and recorded to bind third persons. For a Shreveport parcel in Caddo Parish, that means recording with the parish clerk of court.

More questions about Shreveport, LA Property Tax Guide

Is Shreveport in Caddo or Bossier Parish?

Most of Shreveport is in Caddo Parish, which it serves as parish seat. Parts of the city extend into Bossier Parish.

When is Shreveport property tax due?

Property tax is due December 31 under Louisiana's schedule, and 1% interest per month applies after that. Ask the Caddo Sheriff's tax division for the exact payoff.

How do I pay Caddo Parish property tax?

You can pay online through the Caddo Sheriff's site, where online payments post the same day until 11:59 p.m. You can also visit 501 Texas Street, Room 101.

What is the Louisiana homestead exemption?

The exemption covers $7,500 of assessed value, which is $75,000 of fair market value. Caddo owners can apply through the Assessor's online property search.

Can I sell my Shreveport house if I owe tax?

Yes. The unpaid tax is paid out of the sale proceeds, and the title company needs a payoff figure from the Sheriff.

Where is Lafayette, Louisiana, and what is the land like?

Lafayette is a city of about 121,000 people on the Vermilion River in the Acadiana region of south Louisiana. The 2020 census counted 121,374 residents, which made it the state's fourth most populous city, and the city covers 55.65 square miles of almost entirely dry land.

It lies roughly 59 miles from Baton Rouge, 75 miles from Lake Charles and 135 miles from New Orleans, at an elevation of 36 to 49 feet above sea level. The ground belongs to the southwestern Louisiana Prairie Terrace, which sits higher than the wetlands to the south and west.

According to Wikipedia's summary of the city, Lafayette does not have significant flooding problems apart from local flash flooding. Drainage runs through natural channels including Isaac Verot Coulee, Coulee Mine, Coulee des Poches and Coulee Ile des Cannes, all of which lead to the Vermilion. A seller whose lot backs onto a coulee should expect buyers to ask about drainage and flood insurance.

What is the history behind the city?

Lafayette began as Vermilionville. Jean Mouton, an Acadian settler, gave land for a small Catholic chapel, the site was chosen as the parish seat in 1824, and the Legislature approved incorporation in 1836. The town took the name Lafayette in 1884.

Agriculture, mainly sugar, carried the local economy into the early twentieth century. The university that is now the University of Louisiana at Lafayette was established in 1898 and opened in 1901. Oil was found in the parish in the 1940s, and by 2018 Lafayette had the largest number of oil and natural gas workers in the state.

The city and parish governments consolidated in 1996. Voters split the single council into a city council and a parish council in 2018, though the mayor-president is still elected parishwide. Lafayette Consolidated Government runs public works and land use for the city and for unincorporated areas.

What drives the Lafayette economy?

Energy, health care, education and retail carry the local job market. Wikipedia lists the consolidated city-parish's top employers as of 2021 as the Lafayette Parish School System, Lafayette General Health, Wood Group Production Services, Lafayette Consolidated Government, the University of Louisiana at Lafayette, WHC Inc., Walmart, Our Lady of Lourdes Regional Medical Center, Schlumberger and Stuller Inc.

The area has also become a center for technology, aerospace and banking. That mix helps sellers in two ways. Hospital and university jobs steady housing demand, but a downturn in oil activity can slow it, so timing and certainty of closing matter to anyone selling a house under pressure.

  • Education: the Lafayette Parish School System runs 45 schools, and the University of Louisiana at Lafayette enrolls more than 18,000 students.
  • Community college: South Louisiana Community College is headquartered in the city.
  • Health care: Lafayette General Health joined Ochsner Health, and Our Lady of Lourdes is a major regional hospital.

What is Lafayette's climate, and how does it affect a house?

Lafayette has a humid subtropical climate with rain in every season and heavy summer humidity. NOAA normals for Lafayette Regional Airport show about 62.81 inches of precipitation a year on 117.5 days with measurable rain, and July and August average daily highs above 91 degrees.

The record high is 110 degrees on August 27, 2023, and the record low is 4 degrees on January 22, 2025, so air conditioning and pipe protection both get tested. For a house, that means roofs, attic ventilation, HVAC age and moisture damage are the usual inspection topics.

An older home with a tired roof or a failing compressor can scare off financed buyers, because lenders and appraisers flag those items. Sellers in that position often weigh whether to spend on repairs or sell as-is.

How do you get around Lafayette?

Interstate 10 and Interstate 49 are the main highways, and U.S. 90 and U.S. 167 cross the city under street names such as Evangeline Thruway, Johnston Street and Cameron Street. Ambassador Caffery Parkway forms a partial loop connecting I-10 at Exit 100 on the west with U.S. 90 on the south.

Lafayette Regional Airport is on the southeast side and has scheduled nonstop service to Atlanta, Dallas/Fort Worth, Houston and Charlotte. A new passenger terminal opened on January 20, 2022. The city summary also lists Amtrak's Sunset Limited, which runs three days a week between New Orleans and Los Angeles.

Access to the interstate and to the university and hospital districts shapes which neighborhoods move fastest, and a buyer's commute is one of the first questions a seller hears.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How is city property tax billed in Lafayette?

City tax is billed separately from parish tax. Lafayette Consolidated Government mails city notices at the end of November, and they are delinquent after December 31. After that date the city adds 1% interest per month, and a penalty starts in February.

The city does not accept partial payments, so the full assessment has to be paid at once. You can pay online, walk in at 2701 Moss Street between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. on weekdays, or mail a payment to P.O. Box 4024-C, Lafayette, LA 70502. Cash, check or money order are taken in person, with checks made out to Lafayette Consolidated Government.

Parish taxes are collected by the Sheriff's Office, whose web tax site accepts e-check and major credit cards for a transaction fee. A Lafayette homeowner therefore often holds two bills. Ask your closing agent to confirm both are current before the act of sale.

What happens at the Lafayette tax sale?

The city and parish tax sale takes place online on the first Wednesday in June, and the list is published in the local newspaper on the two Sundays before it.

A home with unpaid taxes that nobody buys at the sheriff's sale becomes adjudicated. Lafayette's adjudicated property FAQ explains that such a property is not owned by the city or parish, and that it has to be adjudicated for three consecutive years before the government will process an application. At any point before the act of sale is recorded, the owner can still redeem by paying all taxes, liens and fees to both collectors.

That redemption right is why selling early is usually cheaper. Each month of delay adds 1% interest and the risk of losing control of the property.

What local code rules should a Lafayette seller know about?

Lafayette Consolidated Government handles property maintenance complaints through its Environmental Quality Division at 337-291-8500, covering long grass, solid waste, hazardous materials and overgrowth. Dilapidated structures go to the Compliance Division at 337-291-8445.

Vacant or inherited houses attract those complaints quickly. Clearing the yard and boarding hazards before listing, or selling to a buyer who takes the property in its current condition, avoids a code notice arriving while you are under contract.

Louisiana does not treat a sale as complete against outsiders until the deed is recorded with the Clerk of Court, so a closing is not done when you sign, only when the act of sale is filed. Our Lafayette Parish clerk guide covers that step in detail.

More questions about Lafayette, LA Property Tax Guide

What is the Lafayette property tax due date?

City notices go out at the end of November and become delinquent after December 31. The parish bill is collected separately by the Sheriff, whose published deadline without penalty is also December 31.

Does Lafayette charge interest on late taxes?

Yes. Lafayette Consolidated Government adds 1% interest per month after December 31, and a penalty starts in February. Partial payments are not accepted on city taxes.

When is the Lafayette tax sale?

It is held online on the first Wednesday in June. The tax sale list is published in the local newspaper on the two Sundays before the sale.

Is Lafayette prone to flooding?

Wikipedia's city summary says Lafayette sits on higher prairie terrace and has no significant flooding apart from local flash flooding, with natural coulees carrying water to the Vermilion River. Check the flood zone for a specific lot.

Can I sell a Lafayette house with unpaid city taxes?

Yes. Unpaid city and parish taxes are paid from the sale proceeds. A buyer who closes as-is can handle a sale with taxes owed.
